title: Etale criterion for geometric connectedness of a fibre
statement: Let $g:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let $s\in S$. The scheme-theoretic fibre $X_s$ [def-pc-scheme-fibre] is geometrically connected [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible] if and only if, for every etale neighbourhood $(U,u)\to(S,s)$, the base-changed fibre $X_u=X\times_SU\times_U\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)$ is connected [def-weil-connected-scheme].

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 37.53.6 (Tag 03GZ, label lemma-characterize-geometrically-connected-fibres, line 15219)

proof.text: Write $k=\kappa(s)$. For an etale neighbourhood $(U,u)\to(S,s)$, the residue-field map $k\to\kappa(u)$ is a finite separable extension by [lem-weil-pbc-etale-residue-field-extension-separable]. Associativity of fibre products identifies the fibre $X_u$ with the base change $X_s\times_{\operatorname{Spec}k}\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(u)$ (the fibre and base-change conventions are [def-pc-scheme-fibre] and [def-pc-base-change]).

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 03GZ, proof, first paragraph (line 15224), with the fibre-product identification written out

proof.text: If $X_s$ is geometrically connected, then its base change along every field extension of $k$ is connected by [def-pc-geometrically-irreducible]. Applying this to the finite separable extension $k\subseteq\kappa(u)$ from Step 1 and using the fibre identification there shows that every etale-neighbourhood fibre $X_u$ is connected.

source.place: More on Morphisms, Lemma 03GZ, proof, first paragraph (line 15224)

proof.text: Conversely, assume every etale-neighbourhood fibre is connected. If $X_s$ were not geometrically connected, [lem-weil-pbc-geometrically-connected-finite-separable-test] would provide a finite separable extension $k\subseteq k'$ for which $X_s\times_k\operatorname{Spec}k'$ is disconnected. By [lem-weil-pbc-etale-neighbourhood-prescribed-residue-field] there is an affine etale neighbourhood $(U,u)\to(S,s)$ whose residue extension $\kappa(u)/k$ is identified with $k'/k$. Under that identification Step 1 identifies $X_u$ with the disconnected base change, contradicting the hypothesis. Therefore $X_s$ is geometrically connected.
